evidence.quote: Today my colleagues on the FOMC and I kept interest rates near zero and maintained our sizable asset purchases.
In terms of tapering, it’s just premature.
Expect us to wait and see and not react if we see small and what we would review—we would view as very likely to be transient effects on inflation.
I’m more concerned about that than about the possibility, which exists, of higher inflation. Frankly, we welcome slightly higher inflation, somewhat higher inflation.
The economy is a long way from our employment and inflation goals, and it is likely to take some time for substantial further progress to be achieved.
the whole focus on exit is premature, if I may say.

parsed.rationale: Powell holds rates at zero and purchases unchanged while stressing patience, dismissing taper and exit talk as premature, welcoming higher inflation and emphasizing downside risks and labor-market slack. The signal is strongly dovish despite an improved second-half outlook.
